newsitem.title: ITALY: IRI reports 1996 profit after Stet transfer. [Corrected 21:36 GMT]
newsitem.headline: IRI reports 1996 profit after Stet transfer. [Corrected 21:36 GMT]

text.p: Italian state industrial holding company IRI said onThursday it made a profit in 1996 for the first time in six years after it slashed debt by transferring ownership of the state telecoms group Stet to the Treasury.
IRI said its parent company made a net profit of 184 billion lire ($110 million) after losing 345 billion lire in 1995.

Net financial indebteness was cut to 9.4 trillion lire from 22.5 trillion and was now approaching a level deemed acceptable under an agreement between the government and the European Union's executive commission, IRI said.
The government has been given until the end of June to cut IRI's debts.

Group consolidated profit was 431 billion lire, compared with 638 billion the previous year (corrects from "a major turnaround after a loss of 207 billion lire the previous year.") The rebound came despite big losses in 1996 at state air carrier Alitalia and defence and electronics group Finmeccanica.
Consolidated financial debt was reduced by around 30 trillion lire to around 26.1 trillion lire, reflecting Stet's exit from the group, IRI said in a statement.
IRI said that over the past four years it had brought down consolidated debt by about 48.5 trillion lire to the current level.

Between July 1992 and December 1996 the group had privatised some 350 companies which had been under its ownership. It raised 24.2 trillion lire through asset sales, excluding the Stet transfer to the Treasury.
IRI said it expected a further improvement in the group's overall performance in 1997 which would be helped by a forecast recovery by Alitalia and Finmeccanica. ($=1,668 lire)
